title: Indirect object pronouns
goal: Use lui and leur to replace à + a person, and put them in the right place in the present, the negative, the futur proche and the passé composé.

items.en: indirect object pronouns: (to) him, her, them

drills.text: Tu parles à Nguyen ? — Oui, je ___ parle tous les jours.
drills.en: Do you talk to Nguyen? — Yes, I talk to him every day.

drills.text: J'écris à mes parents. → Je ___ écris.
drills.en: I write to my parents. → I write to them.

drills.text: Tu téléphones à Lucie ? — Oui, je ___ téléphone ce soir.
drills.en: Are you calling Lucie? — Yes, I'm calling her tonight.
drills.explain: [[téléphoner à]] → indirect → [[lui]], even if English says *call her*.

items.fr: je lui parle / je vais lui parler / je lui ai parlé

drills.prompt: I'm going to call him tomorrow (on the phone).
drills.explain: With aller + infinitive, the pronoun goes before the infinitive: [[je vais lui téléphoner]].
Passé composé: ne + pronoun + avoir + pas: [[je ne lui ai pas répondu]].

options: Je leur ai donné les clés.
Je les ai donné les clés.
drills.explain: In the passé composé, the pronoun goes before avoir: [[je leur ai donné]].

items.note: téléphoner à is indirect (lui/leur); appeler is direct (le/la/les).

items.en: to give someone something as a gift
to answer someone, to reply to someone
What shall we give him / her (as a gift)?
I'm going to ask him / her.

blocks.title: At the office, on Tuesday
blocks.context: Sofia and Alex are preparing Nguyen's birthday 5 à 7.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: C'est l'anniversaire de Nguyen jeudi. Qu'est-ce qu'on lui offre ?
lines.en: It's Nguyen's birthday on Thursday. What shall we give him?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.fr: On pourrait lui offrir un livre de cuisine. Il adore cuisiner.
lines.en: We could give him a cookbook. He loves cooking.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Bonne idée ! Et les gens de l'équipe de Toronto, tu leur as parlé du 5 à 7 ?
lines.en: Good idea! And the people from the Toronto team, have you talked to them about the 5 à 7?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.fr: Pas encore. Je vais leur écrire un courriel ce soir.
lines.en: Not yet. I'm going to write them an email tonight.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Et Raj ? Il est au courant ?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.fr: Je lui ai téléphoné ce matin, mais il ne m'a pas répondu. Je vais lui envoyer un texto.
lines.en: I called him this morning, but he didn't answer me. I'm going to send him a text.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Parfait. Moi, je vais demander à Camille pour la carte. Elle dessine très bien !
lines.en: Perfect. I'm going to ask Camille about the card. She draws really well!

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.fr: Oui, demande-lui. Et surtout, on ne dit rien à Nguyen : on ne lui parle pas du cadeau !
lines.en: Yes, ask her. And above all, we don't say anything to Nguyen: we don't talk to him about the present!

blocks.prompt: In “Qu'est-ce qu'on lui offre ?”, who is lui?
blocks.explain: [[lui]] replaces [[à Nguyen]]: *What shall we give (to) Nguyen?*

blocks.prompt: In “Je vais leur écrire un courriel”, who is leur?
options: The people from the Toronto team
blocks.explain: [[leur]] replaces [[aux gens de l'équipe de Toronto]]: more than one person.

blocks.title: Replacing à + a person
blocks.body:
Many verbs of **communication and giving** are followed by **à + a person**: you talk *to* someone, give something *to* someone. To avoid repeating the person, use an **indirect object pronoun**:

- [[à Nguyen]], [[à Lucie]], [[à mon frère]] → [[lui]] (to him **or** to her)
- [[à mes parents]], [[aux voisins]] → [[leur]] (to them)

[[Je parle à Lucie.]] → [[Je lui parle.]]
[[J'écris à mes parents.]] → [[Je leur écris.]]

You already know the **direct** pronouns [[le, la, les]] from the shopping unit. The difference is simply: is there an **à** before the person?

blocks.title: Direct or indirect?
head: direct (no à)
indirect (à + person)
blocks.note: Good news: [[me, te, nous, vous]] are the same in both columns. You only need to choose for *him, her, them*: [[le / la / les]] or [[lui / leur]].

blocks.title: Verbs with à + person (→ lui / leur)
head: Verb
Example
With a pronoun
rows: Je donne les clés aux voisins.
On offre des fleurs à Lucie.
blocks.note: Also: [[envoyer qqch à]], [[dire qqch à]], [[montrer qqch à]], [[expliquer qqch à]]. Some of these verbs have a thing **and** a person: [[On lui offre des fleurs]] = we give flowers to her.

blocks.title: Where does the pronoun go?
head: Tense
Positive
Negative
rows: Je ne vais pas lui téléphoner.
Je ne lui ai pas téléphoné.
blocks.note: **The rule:** the pronoun goes right **before the verb it belongs to**: before the conjugated verb, before the infinitive, or before [[avoir]] / [[être]] in the passé composé. [[ne]] goes before the pronoun, [[pas]] after the verb or auxiliary.

blocks.title: Classic traps
blocks.body:
- **Téléphoner à = indirect.** English says *call him*, so learners write *je le téléphone*. In French it's [[je lui téléphone]]. But [[appeler]] is direct: [[je l'appelle]]. Both mean *I call him*.
- **Direct verbs (no à in French):** [[aider]] (to help), [[inviter]] (to invite), [[attendre]] (to wait **for**), [[écouter]] (to listen **to**), [[chercher]] (to look **for**). Even when English adds *for* or *to*, French uses le / la / les: [[Je l'aide]], [[Je les attends]], [[Je l'écoute]].
- **Leur never takes -s as a pronoun.** [[Je leur parle]], [[Je leur ai écrit]]. Don't confuse it with the possessive *their*, which agrees with the noun: [[leur fils]] (their son), [[leurs enfants]] (their children).
- **Lui = him or her.** [[Je lui parle]] can mean I talk to him *or* to her. Context tells you which.
- **Wrong place in the passé composé:** *J'ai lui parlé* → [[Je lui ai parlé]].
- **No agreement with lui / leur.** [[Sofia ? Je lui ai écrit.]] The participle [[écrit]] never agrees with an indirect pronoun.

blocks.title: Why so many pronouns?
blocks.body:
French avoids repeating names much more than English does. Compare:

*Did you call your mother? — Yes, I called my mother yesterday.* (OK in English)
[[Tu as téléphoné à ta mère ? — Oui, je lui ai téléphoné hier.]] (natural French)

Repeating [[à ma mère]] sounds heavy in French. So whenever a person has just been mentioned, a pronoun is the natural choice.

examples.fr: Tu as répondu à Karim ? — Non, je ne lui ai pas encore répondu.
examples.en: Did you answer Karim? — No, I haven't answered him yet.

examples.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu vas offrir à tes parents ? — Je vais leur offrir une fin de semaine à Québec.
examples.en: What are you going to give your parents? — I'm going to give them a weekend in Québec City.

blocks.body: **For recognition:** in a positive command, the pronoun comes **after** the verb, with a hyphen: [[Demande-lui !]] (Ask him / her!), [[Téléphone-leur !]] (Call them!). In a negative command it goes back before: [[Ne lui dis rien !]] (Don't tell him / her anything!).

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: [[lui]] is one quick syllable: the *u* glides into the *i*, like [[huit]] without the t.

lines.tip: je lui: say it as one block.
leur and écris are linked: leu-ré-cri.

lines.en: I'm going to call him / her.

lines.fr: Je lui ai offert des fleurs.
lines.tip: offert: the final t is silent, so you hear o-fèr.

lines.fr: Je ne leur ai pas répondu.

blocks.fr: Mes voisins ? Je leur ai donné une clé de mon appartement.
blocks.en: My neighbours? I gave them a key to my apartment.

blocks.fr: Lucie ? Non, je ne lui ai pas encore parlé. Je vais lui téléphoner ce soir.
blocks.en: Lucie? No, I haven't talked to her yet. I'm going to call her tonight.
options: The speaker hasn't talked to Lucie, but will call her tonight.
The speaker called Lucie this morning.
Lucie is going to call the speaker tonight.
blocks.explain: [[je ne lui ai pas encore parlé]] = I haven't talked to her yet; [[je vais lui téléphoner]] = I'm going to call her.

blocks.prompt: A friend asks about your contacts with your family and friends. Answer out loud, using lui or leur each time: When did you last call your parents? Did you write to your best friend this week? What are you going to give your mother (or someone else) for her birthday?
checklist: Je lui ai écrit… / Je ne lui ai pas écrit…

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Mes parents ? Je leur ai téléphoné dimanche, comme chaque semaine. Ma meilleure amie, Nadia, habite à Casablanca. Je lui ai écrit un long message mardi, mais elle ne m'a pas encore répondu. Pour l'anniversaire de ma mère, je vais lui offrir un foulard de Montréal. Elle adore les couleurs !
models.en: My parents? I called them on Sunday, like every week. My best friend, Nadia, lives in Casablanca. I wrote her a long message on Tuesday, but she hasn't answered me yet. For my mother's birthday, I'm going to give her a scarf from Montréal. She loves colours!

blocks.prompt: You're organizing a goodbye party for a colleague who is moving to Vancouver. Write a short message to another colleague: say what you're going to give her or him, who you have already talked to, and who you still need to write to or call. Use lui and leur at least three times.
blocks.promptFr: Écrivez un message à un ou une collègue.
checklist: What you'll give: On va lui offrir…
Who you talked to: J'ai parlé à… / Je leur ai parlé.
Who you haven't contacted: Je ne lui ai pas encore…
A request: Tu peux leur écrire / lui téléphoner ?

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Alex ! Pour le départ de Mei, on va lui offrir un sac à dos et une carte. J'ai parlé aux collègues de Toronto : je leur ai envoyé l'invitation hier. Mais je n'ai pas encore parlé à monsieur Gagnon. Tu peux lui téléphoner demain ? Merci ! Sofia
models.en: Hi Alex! For Mei's leaving party, we're going to give her a backpack and a card. I talked to the colleagues in Toronto: I sent them the invitation yesterday. But I haven't talked to Mr. Gagnon yet. Can you call him tomorrow? Thanks! Sofia

summary:
- Replace **à + one person** with [[lui]] (him or her) and **à + several people** with [[leur]] (no -s)
- Know the verbs with à: [[parler, téléphoner, donner, offrir, écrire, demander, répondre à]] — and that [[aider, appeler, inviter, attendre]] are direct (le, la, les)
- Place the pronoun before the verb, the infinitive or the auxiliary: [[je lui parle]], [[je vais lui parler]], [[je ne lui ai pas parlé]]
